Understanding What AI Can and Cannot Do
AI is penetrating deep into organizations at a very fast pace. A natural concern among all the people is that
“will it replace manual workforce?” To understand this concept fully, it is better to understand one thing – AI
has been created by humans and therefore, AI cannot replace human beings completely.
But still, AI can perform many tasks equally or much better than human beings. Thus, things require careful
investigation and to understand this concept fully, it is very crucial to understand the tasks that AI can perform
on its own and those which require manual intervention.
There are some tasks which can be done by AI on its own, even better than human beings. Human beings are
limited by personal reasons like falling sick, or not producing same quality every time. But that is not the case
This can be classified into “ What AI Does Well in Organisations”. AI systems are particularly effective when
tasks involve large volumes of data and clear patterns. In organisational settings, AI is commonly used for:
1. Automating repetitive and time-consuming activities
2. Analysing large datasets quickly and accurately
3. Identifying trends that may not be visible to human analysts
4. Supporting managers with forecasts and recommendations
These strengths make AI valuable in areas such as accounting, logistics, quality control, and customer support.
But there are numerous tasks which require human intervention. Particularly those tasks that require human
intelligence and varying level of human interventions. This thing poses on AI the limit which can be called as
“ The Limits of Artificial Intelligence”.
Despite its capabilities, AI has important limitations. It does not possess consciousness, emotions, or moral
understanding. AI systems depend entirely on human-designed algorithms and data. They cannot fully grasp
social context, organisational culture, or ethical consequences. As a result, AI lacks the depth of understanding
required for many managerial and human-centred roles. For example, AI cannot judge the relation between
level of excellence and health of that particular employee. It will require every employee to work 100%
efficient by ignoring the medical condition of that employee on that particular day.

Does AI Replace Jobs or Tasks in near future?
Now the basic answer to major concern among all the employees in this world – are they going to be jobless
due to AI? Is the AI going to take all the jobs available to them at a very fast pace? This is the major concern
among the employees, all over the world, be it call centre employees, be it the industry workers, be it the
The answer at present is “NO”, to relief of all the employees. As mentioned in the pervious section, AI is very
efficient but with limitations also. When it comes to social concerns, when it comes emotional intelligence,
when it comes to creative human process etc., there is requirement of human beings is conjunction with AI.
In those particular cases, AI cannot perform the jobs alone. They have to be performed by humans who can
take the help of AI whenever required.
So, it can be said that, AI in those particular situations can be a booster for human decisions and not
replaceable. The replacements of humans are not possible in future also, as far as the current trend is showing.
And, the statement, that has been made in previous section can be repeated once more “ AI has been created
by humans and therefore, AI cannot replace human beings completely”.
We can take two examples for the illustrations given above. First example is of “ Task Automation”. A common
misconception is that AI replaces entire jobs. In reality, most jobs consist of multiple tasks. AI is effective at
handling routine and structured tasks but struggles with non-routine, creative, and interpersonal activities.
Therefore, AI tends to reconfigure jobs rather than eliminate them. For instance, in recruitment, AI can shortlist
candidates based on qualifications, but human managers are needed to assess personality, values, and long-
term potential. This shows that AI supports human work instead of replacing it.
In HR, managers need to interact with lot of employees, each having particular set of traits. Thus, the manager
has to deal with all the employees separately. If this is done by AI, it will fail because it will treat all the
employees as one and deal with them in a uniform manner.
Second example is of “ Creation of New Roles”. The spread of AI has also led to the emergence of new roles
such as AI system supervisors, data analysts, ethics officers, and trainers who teach AI systems how to learn.
Existing roles are evolving, requiring employees to develop new skills and work alongside intelligent systems.

Organisational Implications of AI Adoption
Now, the employees can be little bit relaxed. But not fully. Because of another angle also – the organizational
side. This side also requires serious concern because if there are no organizations, there will be no employees.
The points which organizations need to consider are as follows:
1. Reskilling and Continuous Learning
As AI becomes integrated into work processes, organisations must invest in reskilling and upskilling their
workforce. Employees need to learn how to interpret AI outputs, make informed decisions, and
collaborate effectively with intelligent systems.

Ethical and Social Considerations
AI, if introduced in the organizations, can raise some concerns about the ethical validity of society in general.
The use of AI raises serious ethical and social concerns, including data privacy, workplace surveillance, and
unequal access to opportunities.
The issue was experienced by the author himself. With change in job, with more earning now, he experienced
the increased unwanted phone calls from markets, which advertised their expensive products like estates or
expensive cars, which were absent in the previous job with less earnings.
Without careful governance, AI may reinforce existing inequalities. Human values must therefore guide AI
design and implementation in organisations.
The Future of Work: Humans and AI as Partners
The future of work is best understood as a partnership between humans and AI. AI will act as an intelligent
assistant, handling routine analysis, while humans focus on meaning, purpose, and direction. Employees who
learn to work with AI will become more productive and valuable, not less.
AI is not going to replace humans in organisations. Instead, it is transforming how work is organised and
performed. By automating routine tasks, AI allows humans to focus on higher-level activities such as
leadership, creativity, ethical judgment, and strategic thinking. Organisations that treat AI as a tool for human
enhancement rather than human replacement will be better positioned for sustainable growth. The real
